cells.tense: You are standing here now, and the light you steer by has finished being built.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Take the last few times something you made lit you up, and find the one line they share — what you keep steering toward. Put that line in a sentence. Change nothing because of it.
cells.core:
You've been walking toward something for a while, and it turns out you were carrying it. What you cultivated reached the place it was going, and it shines now without you pushing. That's what this looks like: not a flash, just your own light steady enough to see by.

Where you are now, the shine and the work get confused. You can't tell which part is the finished thing and which is you still tending it. So take the last few times something lit you up and find the one line they share — what you keep steering toward. Put the line in a sentence, and leave the rest alone. The pattern is already yours; your own handwriting just lets you meet it.
cells.sheetLine: You finally shine from what you built, not from wanting.
cells.verb: steering by a light you already carry
cells.place: at the threshold of what you've been clearing room for

cells.tense: You are already shining at a future that hasn't arrived, and your hands are braced for it.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: Before you push the next bright thing forward, pause. Sit with it until the part that truly matters shows itself, and start only with that part. Let the rest of the picture stay open.
cells.core:
There's a light in you and it's running ahead of you. You project it forward — onto next month, onto the thing you're building, onto how it will finally look — and you do it with urgency, like the light has to arrive before it can be trusted. It dazzles more than it warms, and the people near you can feel the difference even if they can't name it.

What's underneath is that you're certain about a future you can't write yet. Nothing needs dimming. Slowing the beam down does. Before you push it forward, pause until the part that truly matters shows itself, and begin there. Only there. What you know directly tends to land cleaner than what you argue into being.
cells.sheetLine: You shine on a future you're bracing for, and it dazzles.

cells.tense: You stand at a threshold you've already crossed, and you no longer expect anything to open.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: Choose the smallest living thing you're carrying and give it ten minutes today — water it, tidy it, sit with it. Ask nothing back from it. That's the whole ask.
cells.core:
You've been cultivating something and it didn't come up. The effort is still going out; the flowering hasn't arrived, and now you stand at a threshold you've already crossed, waiting on an opening you no longer expect. The shine is not the issue. What's run down is the daily care.

What returns first isn't a big blooming, it's something small. Pick the smallest living thing near you — one that's still growing — and give it a few minutes today. Give it what it needs today, not what it was scheduled for. Don't assess it, don't ask it to prove anything, don't decide its future. Care that doesn't clutch feeds a thing that's been left thirsty. Do this for something small enough that you can't fail at it.
cells.sheetLine: You tend a threshold you've already crossed, and nothing flowers.

cells.tense: You are already shining on the people around you, and you don't count it as yours.
cells.act: stay standing in it a while longer
cells.ask: Next time someone thanks you or follows your lead, stay standing there thirty seconds longer than you usually would. Don't deflect, don't explain it away. Just stay put.
cells.core:
People near you are lit by something, and if you told the story you'd leave yourself out of it. The steering you do, the light you carry for the group, the way others find their direction standing next to you — it reads to you as nothing in particular, and to them as the reason they can see.

There's a version of this where the shine has gone quiet and that went unnoticed too. Both are the same gap: you can't see it, whether it's on or off. So don't try to see it by thinking about it. Next time someone thanks you, or follows your lead, or warms — stay where you are thirty seconds past your usual exit. You don't have to believe it. Just don't step out. Holding without forcing means you keep your shape while it's happening.
cells.sheetLine: You're already radiating, and you keep saying you're not.

attempts.check: The record does not say the person's hope was ever actually defeated by a specific event, so the Too Little core must locate them at the door without naming what put them there or what it cost. A reader could object that 'you radiate' is flattery I can't support — it's the signature's own face, not a claim about this person's history, so I'll keep the shine as a thing they've stopped noticing and let them refuse it. The asks survive a wrong read: tracing the pattern, waiting for what matters, tending the small thing, and bearing the next hour are all useful even if the diagnosis misses. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you were never meant to stay ordinary' — cut it.
